To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we discovered two novel crystal forms for Naja naja phosphlipase A2 and solved their structures to 1. 8 A and 2. 65 A, respectively.

we discovered three novel crystal forms for Naja naja phosphlipase A2 including two heretore uncharacterized crystal forms and that the structures of these two new crystal forms reveal trimeric oligomers.
we discovered two new crystal forms of N. naja phospholipe A2 lacking Ca(2+) and solved their structures at 2.65 and 1.8 Angstrom resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the catalytic mechanism and the structural basis of oligomerization of this important enzyme.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the catalytic activity of the Naja phospholipases A(2).
the structural characterization of a phospholipase enzyme, Naja naja phospho-lipase A2, which is involved in the hydrolysis of phospholipids in the cell membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca(2+), which is required for activity, is required for the trimeric association of the Naja phospholipases.
the Ca(2+), in the presence of the substrate, induces a conformational change that allows the enzyme to bind and hydrolyze the lipid substrate.
Ca2+ binding induces a structural change in the Naja naga naja enzyme that allows it to oligomerize into a trimer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the three crystal structures of Naja nuja naja phospholipease A2 provide a structural ensemble from which a detailed understanding of the effects of Ca2+ and oligomerization on structure and catalysis can be derived.

the two new structures, in combination, provide the first detailed structural information about the oligomeric association of Naja n. naja phospholipe A2 and the effects of crystal contacts on the conformation of the enzyme.
the two newly determined structures reveal trimeric association and the tetragonal form reveals tetrameric association, and that Ca2+ is required to stabilize the tetrameric association.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ca(2+), which is required for activity of the enzyme, is not required for crystal formation.
crystal packing can have a profound effect on the oligomeric state of a protein, even when the crystal form is Ca(2+).
the Naja naga naja phospholipease A2 is a unique member of the family of phospholipase molecules and is a useful model for studying the structural changes associated with Ca2+ and oligomerization.
